record.name: Aged Northern Vietnam Ripe Pu-erh Tea
record.origin: Northern Vietnam highlands, on the Yunnan border, Vietnam

paragraphs.text: A loose [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from the highlands of northern Vietnam, where they meet the Yunnan border. It belongs to a trade that has long run across that border. For generations, houses in Hong Kong and Guangzhou bought leaf from the Vietnamese side and made it into pu’er style tea, and this lot comes from that lineage.

The leaf was [heaped warm and damp](shou:wet-piling) so heat, moisture and microbes could work through it, then left loose to age rather than pressed. The method is the usual one for the style. What sets this tea apart is where the leaf grew.

brewing.text: Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, sweet cup with earthy or woody notes. A young ripe tea can carry a faint smell of the pile, which fades with airing or in the first steeps.
